findings.claim: The app comparison can report identical bundles when assets are served at incorrect paths or additional assets are embedded.
findings.evidence: compareWithApp checks only bySha.has(file.sha256) or htmls.some(...), then constructs the app digest using the web build's paths and hashes through served.push(file). It never verifies the app's path-to-content mapping or rejects extra assets. Swapping two asset mappings leaves this check passing despite violating VS-2 bundle identity.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare independently obtained app asset paths and contents with the complete web manifest, rejecting missing, extra and incorrectly mapped assets.

findings.claim: HTML normalization treats behaviorally different documents as identical.
findings.evidence:
normalizeHtml applies replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim() to every text token and discards whitespace-only tokens. Consequently, '
a  b
' and '
a b
' compare equal; inline JavaScript string literals with different whitespace also compare equal. compareWithApp substitutes the original web hash whenever sameHtml returns true, masking these content changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Use HTML-aware parsing and restrict normalization to proven serialization differences, preserving significant whitespace and raw script/style contents; add negative controls for these collisions.

findings.claim: Detected renames are overlaid without removing their original paths, so negative controls can test a different source tree from the candidate.
findings.evidence: captureCandidate obtains tracked paths with git diff --name-only -z HEAD --. When Git detects a rename, this lists the destination rather than both paths. applyCandidate overlays that destination onto a HEAD checkout, leaving the old tracked file present. The subsequent captureCandidate digest comparison only checks the original working tree and cannot detect the extra scratch file.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable rename detection when collecting paths with --no-renames, or parse rename statuses and explicitly record deletion of each source path. Verify the resulting scratch tree against the captured candidate.

findings.claim: Applying a candidate can write outside the scratch checkout through a symlink ancestor.
findings.evidence: applyCandidate creates captured symlinks and subsequently calls rmSync, writeFileSync and chmodSync on joined paths without checking ancestor containment. For a tracked directory replaced by an absolute symlink, captureCandidate can include both the new directory symlink and its formerly tracked child paths; lstatSync follows intermediate symlinks. Sorted application creates the symlink before processing those children, directing deletion and writes into its external target. This contradicts the isolation guarantee and can breach reference-repo-read-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply deletions before creating symlinks, reject overlays containing descendants of symlink entries, and verify that every mutation's resolved parent remains inside the scratch checkout.
